7. [RARC.5.6.8] Delivers the input's event and every derived event,
   internal and action alike, to the stream callback in the order they were
   processed ([RARC.5.8]).

   **Processed means propagated, per action.** Each RHS action's change to
   working memory is propagated through the network, truth-maintenance
   retractions included, before the change is recorded and before the next
   action of the same firing runs. A cascade retraction is therefore
   recorded ahead of the assert that caused it, and a firing that emits
   twice, where only the second emit invalidates a `no (...)`, records the
   retraction between its two asserts. Stream order is processing order,
   not causal order; a reader that takes precedence for causation
   attributes every cascade to the wrong cause.

   This is a rule's action. A host input is recorded on arrival, before
   what its evaluation produces ([RFCS.6.7]), and an engine withdrawal
   before the withdrawals it cascades into ([RFCS.7a.4], [LFST.7.3.6]).
